task.title: Stay Safe on Wi-Fi Networks
task.shortdesc: Follow these recommendations to stay safe on Wi-Fi networks.

step.p: A VPN encrypts your internet connection, making it much harder for hackers to intercept your data. Always use a trusted VPN service when connecting to public Wi-Fi.
For important accounts (such as email and banking), enable multi-factor authentication. This adds an extra layer of protection, even if your password is compromised.
Refrain from logging into sensitive accounts or making online purchases while connected to public Wi-Fi. Wait until you're on a trusted, secure network.
Ensure the websites you visit are secure by checking that they begin with HTTPS rather than HTTP. A padlock symbol in the address bar indicates a secure connection.
Public networks make it easier for others to access your device if file-sharing or printer-sharing features are enabled. Turn these features off in your system settings while on public Wi-Fi.
Most devices have an option to automatically connect to available Wi-Fi networks. Disabling this feature can prevent your device from connecting to insecure or rogue networks without your knowledge.
Ensure that your operating system, browser, and security software are up to date. Software updates often contain security patches that protect against newly discovered threats.

cmd.b: Stay up to date on NC State Cybersecurity Training:

step.p: NC State Cybersecurity Training is required for all employees and new undergraduate students beginning in October 2026. It is highly encouraged for all students, staff, and faculty to go through the training to educate themselves on cybersecurity issues.
